answer.rationale: Memory c2 suggests the low-cost vendor cut unit cost sharply and had accurate invoicing, but the memory is now 33 days old and was written before the current 18% cut mandate and the line's 94% utilization with no buffer. I need to confirm the archived record before committing. If verified, I switch primary supply to the low-cost vendor because they already meet the cost mandate alone and their history shows quick onboarding. The 14-day contract expiry forces a decision now; deferring risks a supply gap on a line with no buffer. Adding a second source is attractive for resilience but I have capacity for exactly one decision, and cost is the binding constraint this cycle. I note the risk that the line has no buffer during any transition, so the switch must include a 14-day overlap clause to keep the incumbent supplying until the low-cost vendor's first delivery is confirmed. Memory c6's volume-pricing lesson and c4's renegotiation lesson are relevant but deferred to the next review cycle.
